note: Online college test preparation and admissions counselling, Palo Alto. Kaplan (Washington Post) bought its business in January 2002 (Chronicle of Higher Education: https://www.chronicle.com/article/kaplan-buys-achieva-and-3-vocational-colleges/) and carried it on: acquired. Round not named.

Internet business-to-business payments, Portland ME. Filed for Chapter 11 in November 2002 'in connection with its sale to Fleet National Bank' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1109190/000095015304000638/p68904e10vk.htm): a sale out of bankruptcy, defunct. Round not named.

Enterprise application integration software, Redwood Shores. Its assets were sold to DataMirror in September 2000 for $15M, which went to its debts, and its investors wrote off their equity (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1036052/000092701603000294/d10k.txt): defunct. Round not named.

Voice-over-DSL gateways and softswitches, Santa Clara. The Heico Companies took control in October 2003 (EE Times: https://www.eetimes.com/heico-takes-contol-of-struggling-coppercom/): acquired. Round not named.

Online recruiting for mid-level professionals, Palo Alto. Acquired by Spencer Stuart in January 2001 (https://www.onrec.com/news/news-archive/spencer-stuart-acquires-cruel-world-012001). Round not named.

Digital media incubator, Los Angeles, later the owner of the AVP beach volleyball tour: it merged into its subsidiary AVP in 2003 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/930817/000114420406015387/v038767_10ksb.txt), and AVP stopped operating in August 2010 and went bankrupt: defunct. Round not named.

Shaquille O'Neal's online footwear and apparel store, Santa Monica. Cut staff from about 50 to under 20 in October 2000 and shut down (Los Angeles Business Journal: https://labusinessjournal.com/news/internet-shaqs-web-play-falters/): defunct. TCV and SportsLine funded its first round of about $20M; the round is not named by letter.

CRM customer-data integration software (eMerge), Longmont CO. TCV led the $34M second round of August 2000 (BizWest, 2000-08-11): a Series B, Growth. Sold in 2002 (PitchBook names Seurat Company, Crunchbase Boulder Ventures; neither page could be read): acquired, buyer unconfirmed.

Web integration and IT consulting, Portland OR. Filed for Chapter 11 in October 2001 and was bought out of bankruptcy by SBI (Deseret News: https://www.deseret.com/2001/10/18/19612168/salt-lake-based-sbi-buys-bankrupt-emerald-solutions/): defunct. Consulting is outside the focus taxonomy. Round not named.

Telecom network engineering services, Richardson TX. Its CEO left in 2003 and still sat on its board in 2004 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1123028/000119312504100220/dex991.htm); no closing or sale found: status unknown. Services are outside the focus taxonomy. Round not named.

Business-to-business online communities for trade associations, Bellevue WA. No trace after the early 2000s; CB Insights marks it dead (https://www.cbinsights.com/company/esociety): defunct. Round not named.

Online entertaining and party-supplies store founded by two Quicken.com staff, San Francisco (Forbes, 2000: https://www.forbes.com/forbes/2000/0911/6607248a.html). No closing or sale found: status unknown. Round not named.

Home-repair contractor matching, Beaverton OR (with a Denver office until 2001). CB Insights records it acquired in 2001 without naming the buyer (https://www.cbinsights.com/company/handyman-online): acquired, buyer unknown. Round not named.

Online wholesale mortgage exchange (IMX Exchange), San Ramon CA, later Houston. Its withdrawn 2000 S-1 shows TCV entering at the Series C and buying again in the D and E: Growth. After a 2002 alliance with LION, Inc. no trace of a sale or closing: status unknown (probably a quiet wind-down).

IP multi-service broadband access equipment, Chelmsford MA. Acquired by Telco Systems in July 2005 (Telecompaper: https://www.telecompaper.com/news/integral-access-acquired-by-telco-systems--482439). Round not named.

Corporate barter and business-to-business digital-currency exchange, Stamford CT. Allied Capital, a fellow holder, booked a realized loss on it in 2002 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/3906/000095013306000223/w16837e497.htm); no closing or sale found: status unknown. Round not named.

Mobile-commerce platform for carriers, San Francisco (Sunil Paul's LiveMind, founded 1999, per later SEC biographies: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1079270/000092838501500568/d10ka.txt). No closing or sale found: status unknown. Round not named.

Managed hosting for business web applications, San Mateo. Left the hosting business abruptly in May 2001 (a customer's 10-QSB: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1013690/000095017001500226/m32968.txt) and later went bankrupt: defunct. Round not named.

Optical networking equipment, San Jose. Shut down, with a hired officer winding the company up from May 2003 to March 2004 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1322387/000139390507000160/itli_8k.htm): defunct. Round not named.

Metro optical switching (Unifier), San Jose. Ended its merger with Ariel in October 2001 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/911167/000091116702000003/withdrawalletterascii.txt) and still existed in a 2003 arbitration; no closing or sale found: status unknown. Round not named.

Carrier-class voice-over-IP switching, Cupertino. Its last CFO served April to July 2002 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1016243/000091205702034761/a2088522zdef14a.htm); no closing or sale found: status unknown. Round not named.
Application development tools (NatStar, NS-DK), Paris with a US operation in Washington DC. Acquired by Cognicase of Canada in 1998 (https://www.chapsvision.com/en-us/about-us/). Round not named.

Foreign-exchange payment and settlement services (formerly Sonnet Financial), San Mateo. Sold to Commonwealth Foreign Exchange in September 2002 (PitchBook, read only in a search result): acquired. Round not named.

Web-based mortgage origination software, Sunrise FL (2001). MeridianLink bought OpenClose for $61.8M in cash in November 2022 (MeridianLink's 10-K for 2022: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834494/000183449423000026/mlnk-20221231.htm): acquired. Round not named.

Enterprise software, Mountain View (a 2001 General Magic release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/933524/000109581101504858/f75723ex99-1.htm). No closing or sale found: status unknown. Round not named.

Online home-improvement store backed by Ace Hardware, Evanston IL. Stopped selling in 2001, after which Amazon bought the remaining assets and brand (https://www.failory.com/amazon/ourhouse-com): defunct. Round not named.

Video security and loss-prevention systems, Andover MA. Acquired by Pavion in April 2023 (CB Insights, whose profile lists TCV: https://www.cbinsights.com/company/lp-network). Security installation services are outside the focus taxonomy. Round not named.
Cash-back online shopping network, Malvern PA (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/729976/000101041201000063/0001010412-01-000063.txt). No trace after 2001: defunct. Round not named.

Online swapping marketplace for consumer goods, San Francisco. No trace after 2001; CB Insights marks it dead (https://www.cbinsights.com/company/switchouse): defunct. The sources disagree on TCV's round letter: not named.
Automated product-verification software for communications equipment makers, Santa Clara. Merged into QuikCycle in October 2001 (PitchBook, read only in a search result): acquired. Round not named.

Cloud e-procurement software, Charlotte NC. Operating in 2009 (Lawson's 10-K) and acquired by Basware in March 2016 (SDCExec: https://www.sdcexec.com/sourcing-procurement/news/12189030/basware-inc-basware-acquires-verian-a-cloudbased-purchasetopay-provider). Round not named.
